MCA — Middle East Combat Arena

Offline single-player skirmish RTS · single-file build · v0.9.0

What it is

MCA is a single-player skirmish RTS set in a near-future Middle East conflict. You start with one MCV; deploy it, build power and oil income, raise a combined-arms force from your faction's real-world order of battle (161 units and 35 structures across 9 factions), and destroy the enemy AI's Construction Yard and MCV. Skirmish vs 1+ AI opponents, with an optional AI ally for 2v2. Everything is procedural — no downloads, no accounts, no network.

How to run

Double-click MCA.html. That's it — no install, no server, no internet. The entire game (code, data, art, sound) is inside that one file; share it by email/chat as-is. It runs in any modern browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) straight from disk.
  • MCA.html — the game.
  • MCA_Reference.html — the full unit / structure / counter reference.
  • README.html — this file.

Sound starts after your first click or keypress — browsers block audio before a user gesture, that's normal. See Troubleshooting if anything looks off.

How a match works

1. Select your MCV and press D (or double-click it) to deploy the Construction Yard.
2. Build from the bottom bar: Power Plant first, then an Oil Depot next to an oil field (gold rings show them while placing), then production structures.
3. Structures must sit within the build-radius circle of your base. If you click a slightly-off spot, placement snaps to the nearest legal cell; if nothing nearby works, a red label at the cursor says why. Hold Shift while placing to chain multiple defenses.
4. Watch the power dot in the top bar — green is fine, amber is close to the limit, red means low power (production slows).
5. Left-click (or right-click) the map with a production structure selected to set a rally point — fresh units auto-move there.

Factions

Nine playable factions, each with its own real-world order of battle, an economy perk, and a signature ability (active abilities need their unique structure — the button tells you which). The setup strip scrolls like a deck of cards — drag it, flick it, or use the ‹ › arrows:

EgyptDepth / mix · cheap CY rebuild · Sa'ka Insertion (needs Sa'ka Tent)
SaudiAltitude / quality · +oil income · RSAF Tasking (needs Green Crescent)
UAEScalpel / precision · fast early build · Edge Network (passive)
AlgeriaWeight / bubble · cheaper vehicles · Integrated Sky (passive)
TurkeyDrone mesh · Siha Mesh (passive)
IsraelShield + knife · Iron Layer (passive)
IndiaScale + BrahMos · BrahMos Lane (needs Cruise Battery)
PakistanFirst strike · fast Babur build · Babur Window (needs Ghaznavi Rain)
IranSwarm + rain · Shahed Rain (needs Drone Workshop)

AI opponents pick a personality — Auto (adaptive) (the default: re-reads the battle every few seconds and flips doctrine — air-heavy vs air spam, turtles when out-gunned, presses when ahead, harasses when even), Balanced Assault (front), Air Superiority (sky), Hit & Run (raid), Fortress Defense (fortress) — and a difficulty: Easy (recruit), Normal (veteran), Hard (elite), Expert (marshal). Add up to the map's spawn count, or tick the ally box for a 2v2.

Research upgrade kits new

Each faction has 3 researchable upgrade kits (27 total) — e.g. Egypt's Misr rifle refit, Abrams SEP kit and F-16V Block 70. Research a kit at its producer structure (barracks, war factory or airfield, shown on the button) for a one-time credit cost: the affected unit line gains roughly +20% HP and +20–25% damage, applied both to units already on the field and to everything trained afterwards. Each kit can be bought once per match — hover the button for cost and targets.

Empty QuarterUp to 6 players, huge open desert.
Suez Convoy Raid newThe canal is the only crossing. Hold a bank, deny the bridges, and raid the convoy route. Water splits the map — air and navy matter.
Golan Heights newWest is open desert. East is the rocky plateau. Two passes cut the escarpment — take the high ground or die on the approach.
Hormuz Blockade newA narrow strait and three islands. Navy owns the water, batteries own the shores. Whoever closes the lane wins the oil.

Also new: the in-game chrome wears a desert-military skin — gold-framed panels, an inset top bar, and warm panel fills.

Tips

  • Income comes from Oil Depots — each one spawns its own harvester. Expand early, defend them; kill an enemy harvester and their income stalls.
  • Use stances: hold ground keeps tanks on a ridge line; hold fire keeps stealthy raiders from revealing themselves; Shift+right-click queues waypoints so you can route around defenses.
  • Hover any build tile for cost, build time, HP, and what beats it / threatens it.
  • Engineers repair your buildings — and can capture enemy or neutral ones: order them to attack the structure and hold the 2-second channel.
  • Lose your Construction Yard? You get one rebuild — keep some credits in reserve.
  • The Command / Tech structure (SH-08) unlocks the expensive tier-2/3 units.
  • Superweapons charge for 5 minutes once built — the button lives in the build bar's right column.
  • The EVA voice lines speak your faction's language (Arabic dialects, French, Turkish, Hebrew, Farsi, Hindi, Urdu). Music is off by default — enable it in the menu; M mutes everything.
  • Each faction plays differently — read the identity line on the faction picker. The full unit/structure reference is in MCA_Reference.html.

Troubleshooting

  • No sound? Browsers block audio until you click or press a key — interact once. Check you're not muted (M) and the menu volume slider is up. Voice lines need a system voice for the faction's language; if none is installed the browser falls back or stays silent — the game is unaffected.
  • Blank screen / won't start? Use a current Chrome, Edge or Firefox. Very old browsers without ES-module support won't run the dev version, but MCA.html is built to run from file:// as-is — if your browser blocks local files, try another browser rather than a server.
  • Settings lost between sessions? Volume, mute and music preference are stored in the browser's local storage; private/incognito windows discard them on close. That's expected.
  • Slow on a big map? Drop to 1x speed, zoom out less, or close other tabs. The whole sim is deterministic — lag only affects rendering, never game outcomes.
  • Edge pan not working? It pauses while the game is paused or a menu overlay is open, and while the pointer is outside the window. Use arrows or middle-drag instead.
  • Where are saves? There are none by design — skirmishes are meant to be played in one sitting (roughly 15–40 minutes). Closing the tab or navigating away mid-match asks for confirmation, since the match would be lost.

Credits

Design, orders of battle, stats and counter matrix from the ASH-SHARQ design sheets (attachments/: gdd_v02.docx, stat_sheet.xlsx and the extracted CSV set). Code, greybox art, sound and music: vanilla JS + Canvas 2D + WebAudio, no dependencies, fully offline.

MCA.html is the shareable single-file build, generated by tools/build_singlefile.py. The dev version (client/ + local server) is unchanged; see START_GAME.bat for the dev workflow.
